response.sql: SELECT c.zoneref, s.insurstat, COUNT(*) AS record_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS record_fraction FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY c.zoneref, s.insurstat ORDER BY record_fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The schema uses PostgreSQL-style syntax, so NULLS LAST and window functions are supported.
The inner join drops conservation records whose zoneref has no matching sites.zoneregistry. The denominator is the count of all matched conservation records.
A missing insurance status means SQL NULL. Empty strings are not treated as missing. SQL GROUP BY places all NULL statuses in one group, which is kept as its own value.

The fraction is never NULL, so NULLS LAST has no effect. The 'missing last' instruction is read as applying to the sort, and the NULL-status group is ranked only by its fraction. If the instruction means the NULL-status group must go last regardless of fraction, use the alternative.

alternatives.interpretation: Force the rows with a missing insurance status to the bottom of the result, regardless of their fraction, and sort all other rows by fraction from highest to lowest. Then keep the top 10.
alternatives.sql: SELECT c.zoneref, s.insurstat, COUNT(*) AS record_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS record_fraction FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY c.zoneref, s.insurstat ORDER BY (s.insurstat IS NULL), record_fraction DESC LIMIT 10;
